title: Tensor exactness and kernel flatness for a flat-quotient sheaf sequence
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Let $0\to F\to G\to H\to0$ be a short exact sequence of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], meaning a monomorphism followed by an epimorphism with image equal to kernel. Suppose $H$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For every sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $N$, the sequence $0\to F\otimes_{\mathcal O}N\to G\otimes_{\mathcal O}N\to H\otimes_{\mathcal O}N\to0$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is short exact. If $G$ is also flat, then $F$ is flat.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], tensoring is additive and has a right adjoint in each variable. It preserves cokernels: under the adjunction, maps out of the tensor of a cokernel correspond exactly to maps out of the original middle object annihilating the original first map. Thus tensoring is right exact. The same cited statement gives the natural symmetry $X\otimes Y\cong Y\otimes X$; its naturality identifies the maps in the two tensor orientations, so the exactness defining flatness can be used in either variable. Apply [lem-pc-sites-modules-functorial-flat-cover] to $N$ to obtain an epimorphism $P\to N$ with $P$ flat, and put $Q=\ker(P\to N)$. Hence $0\to Q\to P\to N\to0$ is short exact in the abelian category of module sheaves.

Form the tensor diagram whose rows are $F\otimes Q\to G\otimes Q\to H\otimes Q\to0$, $0\to F\otimes P\to G\otimes P\to H\otimes P\to0$, and $F\otimes N\to G\otimes N\to H\otimes N\to0$. The first and third rows and all columns are right exact by step 1. The middle row is short exact because $P$ is flat; the map $H\otimes Q\to H\otimes P$ is mono because $H$ is flat, using the natural tensor symmetry of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. Here is the left-injectivity chase, written with generalized elements: for $x$ in the kernel of $F\otimes N\to G\otimes N$, lift $x$ to $a$ in $F\otimes P$. The image of $a$ lifts from $b$ in $G\otimes Q$. The image of $b$ in $H\otimes Q$ is zero, since its image in $H\otimes P$ is zero and that vertical map is mono. Lift $b$ from $c$ in $F\otimes Q$. Subtract the image of $c$ from $a$; its image in $G\otimes P$ vanishes, so the middle-row mono makes the difference zero. Thus $x=0$. Each lift means pullback along the indicated epimorphism, which is again epi in an abelian category; equality after these epic refinements implies equality before them. This is the explicit snake-lemma chase of 03EX, valid without assuming enough points or sectionwise surjectivity. Together with right exactness it proves the first assertion.

Now assume $G$ is flat and let $U\to V$ be any monomorphism of module sheaves. Step 2 gives monomorphisms $F\otimes U\to G\otimes U$ and $F\otimes V\to G\otimes V$. The composite $F\otimes U\to G\otimes U\to G\otimes V$ is mono because $G$ is flat, using the natural tensor symmetry of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. It also factors as $F\otimes U\to F\otimes V\to G\otimes V$, so $F\otimes U\to F\otimes V$ is mono. Thus tensoring with $F$ preserves all monomorphisms and is right exact by step 1. For an arbitrary short exact sequence, right exactness gives image equal to kernel and epimorphy of the last map, and preservation of its first mono gives left exactness. It is therefore exact, proving flatness of $F$ by its definition.
